title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos

claims.text: India's telecom regulator TRAI now requires caller-ID apps to send user spam reports to a blockchain-based platform run by telecom operators.
evidence_terms: blockchain-based platform maintained by telecom operators

claims.text: Truecaller calls the requirement a one-way exchange that is anti-competitive and transfers commercially valuable data to telecom operators.
India is Truecaller's largest market, with well over 350 million monthly active users.

scenes: Wide shot. The presenter looks into the camera and opens the segment. A lower-third graphic reads 'India: Caller-ID apps must share spam reports'. A stylized map of India appears on screen with a phone icon flagged as spam.

Medium shot as the camera slowly pushes in on the presenter. An on-screen diagram shows an app icon sending a report arrow to a blockchain graphic labeled 'Telecom operators platform', with the label 'TRAI' above it.

Medium shot. The presenter gestures toward a floating graphic. A quote card reads 'One-way exchange, anti-competitive: Truecaller' and a stat counter animates to '350M+ monthly active users in India'. The graphic fades as the segment closes.
script: If you use a caller-ID app in India, your spam reports are about to travel further. Telecom regulator TRAI now requires apps like Truecaller to send user spam reports to a blockchain-based platform run by telecom operators. Truecaller calls it a one-way exchange that is anti-competitive, handing commercially valuable data to telcos. India is its largest market, with well over 350 million monthly active users.

news.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
news.summary: Truecaller says the one-way sharing requirement would hand a commercially valuable proprietary asset to telecom operators.
